entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Prince Ludwig Joseph Maximilian von Starhemberg (1762–1833) was a pivotal Austrian diplomat whose career spanned the tumultuous era of the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars, culminating in the post-Congress of Vienna European order. As a scion of one of the Habsburg monarchy's most distinguished noble families, his influence extended through key European capitals, shaping Austria's foreign policy responses to unprecedented continental upheaval. Elevated to a Knight of the Order of the Golden Fleece in 1802, Starhemberg embodied the aristocratic diplomacy that sought to restore monarchical legitimacy and power in the face of revolutionary republicanism and imperial ambition.

Starhemberg's most significant posting was as Austrian ambassador to the United Kingdom, serving in London from 1793 to 1807. During this critical period, he tirelessly worked to forge and sustain anti-French coalitions, a cornerstone of Habsburg foreign policy against the First French Republic and later Napoleon's empire. His diplomatic efforts were instrumental in securing British subsidies and military cooperation for Austria's war efforts, navigating the complex web of alliances and betrayals that characterized the early 19th century. Later, he played a role in the Congress of Vienna (1814–1815), contributing to the territorial and political restructuring of Europe alongside figures like Metternich and Castlereagh.
